description.narrative: In July 2020, the Ministry of Economy, through the Secretariat of Labour Inspection, instituted an internal working group to develop a national campaign on the rights of migrant and refugee workers during the pandemic of COVID-19. After consultations with civil society organizations and the articulation of partnerships with multilateral organizations, the "Proteja o Trabalho" campaign was launched in September 2020. The Campaign provides, on a permanent basis and through government channels, quality information services (such as publications, guides, training and audio-visual materials regarding rights and social protection schemes) so that migrant and refugee workers and employers can carry out their activities safely, both from a legal point of view and from a biosafety point of view, given the advent of the pandemic. This information was also used by labour inspectors to provide legal services to migrants at the local units of the Ministry of Economy (linked to the Labour Inspection Secretariat). The Campaign's website allows for 9 booklets to be downloaded, covering the following topics: 1) Emergency Program; 2) Emergency Employment and Income Preservation Benefit; 3) Digital Work Registration; 4) Prevention Measures; 5) Learning for Young People; 6) People with Disabilities; 7) Pregnant woman's rights; 8) Child Labour; and 9) Slave Labour. On the website it is also possible to find the records of 9 Lives held on the same topics, in partnership with the National School of Labour Inspection (ENIT). Finally, the site features the series of 9 short videos "Ser Brasil Migrantes e Refugiados" (produced and broadcasted under the Campaign, in June 2021), as well as the possibility of filing a complaint in case of irregular situations suggestive of forced or child labour. All materials have translations in English, Spanish, French, Arabic and Creole. The ILO supported the efforts of the Federal Government from the outset, having participated in the working group formed, alongside with IOM and UNHCR. ILO provided technical inputs for the preparation of the booklets, as well as for the organization of live online events. There was significant participation of labour inspectors during these events, and that fulfilled the function of training these public agents (who work throughout the national territory) with regard to the legislation in force under COVID-19, especially in the case of migrants and refugees. The ILO also acted in defining the Campaign's communication strategy (including suggesting the name finally adopted by the Campaign) and hired the company responsible for producing the short videos. The ILO led the production process along side with the labour inspectors, the local partners (which had direct contact with the identified characters) and the other bodies involved (such as the press office of the Ministry of Economy and the other UN agencies). An agreement was also concluded with Canal Futura (paid TV channel) so that the videos were broadcasted on this national chain during prime time, reaching a wide audience beyond migrants and refugees.

description.narrative:
In June 2021, the Government, under the leadership of the Ministry of Economy, adopted two new OSH strategies: one aiming at decreasing occupational accidents in Small and Micro Enterprises; and the second on the road transportation sector, aiming at enhancing occupational safety and health of self-employed truck drivers. Both strategies integrate awareness raising material to provide the target groups knowledge management activities to prevent accidents and injuries and capacity-building courses on the existing legal framework. In May 2020, the Government launched a self-diagnostic tool, in line with federal government's digital transformation program, to amplify compliance with OSH legislation. The online tool allows the assessment of a company's OSH situation and the development of improvement plans according to the characteristics of the business and the risks mapped in the self-diagnosis. The tool has been of great support to assist employers in adapting to and complying with legal requirements, measures, and precautions related to COVID-19. It provided a better understanding of Brazilian Legislation to many SMEs. Two modules help employers to check if their enterprises complies with the ordinances 19 and 20, two of the main OSH legislation adopted in 2020, which establish the standards that companies should follow regarding Covid-19 prevention. The tool integrates the Risk Management Program (RMP), which is a self-management tool on occupational risks aimed at SMEs. This online instrument adopted and disseminated by the Government will enable higher rates of compliance with and will help to reinforce the existing OSH standards at SMEs in Brazil. It allows the entrepreneurs themselves to generate RMP reports free of charge, interactively and online, through a web platform. This tool aims at reducing the number of occupational hazards and diseases in the business segment, through the employer's awareness of the risks existing in their work environment. With the support of RBSA funds, the ILO developed two studies to support the revision and elaboration of the national OSH strategies for two sectors - Small and Micro Enterprises (SMEs); and road transportation -, launched in September 2021. The two studies are: "Relatório técnico com análises e sistematizações sobre o cenário de SST no Brasil com foco nas MPEs", focused on Small and Micro Enterprises; and "Relatório técnico com análises e sistematizações sobre o cenário de SST no Brasil no setor de transporte rodoviário com foco em caminhoneiros autônomos", focused on self-employed truck drivers and their OSH reality. The ILO reinforced the implementation of the strategies by conducting two campaigns on risk prevention for both sectors.
Under the Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with the Special Secretariat for Social Security and Labour (SEPRT), signed in 2020, the ILO supported the development and design of the integrated digital tools: the self-diagnosis and the Risk Management Program. With the financial support of Brazil, the ILO provided technical services for the design of the self-diagnostic tool on OSH businesses compliance as well as for the occupational risk assessment tool for (SMEs). During the design phase, the ILO regularly consulted the Ministry of Economy and its Labour Secretariat in order to provide technical inputs so that the final design of the tools would fit the Government´s needs.

description.narrative: The Program "TODAS in-Rede" aiming at financial independence of vulnerable populations was implemented in five municipalities of the state of São Paulo, targeting women with disabilities, including transgender and afro-descendants as priority groups. Participants built their capacities in several areas, such as labour market, health (including HIV issues) and sexuality. "TODAS in-Rede" is an innovative program because of its inter-sectoral approach. It has 4 pillars: 1. increase the number of women with disabilities in the labour market, promoting inclusion, professional training, technical support, and first employment; 2. inform women with disabilities about their sexual and reproductive rights; 3. prevent violence, considering that women with disabilities are more vulnerable to violence, especially those afro-descendants or LGBTI; 4. empower and promote leadership skills for women with disabilities. This project develop several actions, including professional training and on line courses, besides support to the municipalities to develop policies in this area. The ILO trained São Paulo state civil servants responsible for implementing the "TODAS in-rede" project, on how to develop policies to include people with disabilities in the formal labour market. The ILO partnered with the Labour Prosecutor´s Office (MPT) and designed a free online course with four modules. The course was prepared so as to integrate gender, sexual orientation, gender identity and race as a key part of the discussion.
